# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

# Apple HIG: Platform and task adaptation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and

1. Identify the person’s primary task and the target platform before translating a screen. Read that platform’s procedure; use Principles to resolve hierarchy and Designing for games only for gameplay.

name: apple-hig-designing-for-ipados
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an iPad experience for resizable multitasking, a larger canvas, mixed input, or prolonged creative work.

# Use the iPad canvas without assuming exclusive space

Read [Designing for iPadOS](../../references/designing-for-ipados.md). Inspect the task, related content, current navigation, window assumptions, and supported touch/Pencil/keyboard/pointer paths. Identify whether people hold the iPad or work at a stand/table. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode and revise only the authorized surface using the existing stack.

Decide which relationships benefit from simultaneous visibility. Keep a list beside detail or tools beside a canvas when that reduces navigation; leave unrelated information out. Replace repeated full-screen transitions or modal panels with persistent contextual structure when space permits. At compact multitasking widths, collapse that structure while retaining selection, draft, and the route back to context.

Map each meaningful operation to the inputs the task supports. Touch remains usable without attached accessories. Precise pointer selection and keyboard commands can accelerate work; Pencil may create or annotate content without becoming a required substitute for ordinary controls. Let input methods change during the same task without discarding state or hiding essential commands behind hover.

For cross-app work, specify what can be dragged out/in and where imported content lands. Treat resizing, orientation, larger text, and another app's presence as normal operating conditions. If the iPad experience runs on Mac, identify the Mac adaptation work rather than claiming identical behavior is already native.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a sheet-music editor copies its phone flow: choose score, open full-screen tools, then return to the page after each change. Decision: editing needs score and tools together, but multitasking may narrow the window. After, a contextual tool column accompanies the score at regular width and becomes a dismissible panel at compact width, preserving page, selection, and undo history. Touch editing and keyboard commands reach the same operations.

Deliver a wide/narrow task flow and input mapping or corresponding implementation. Fail if shrinking loses a selected object, a pointer-only control blocks touch, or imported content silently replaces work. Use supplied evidence for findings; physical reach, Pencil response, and inter-app drag/drop remain unverified until exercised on supported devices.

Continue with [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md) for resizing, [Apple Pencil and Scribble](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-apple-pencil-and-scribble/SKILL.md) for drawing/writing, or [Pointing devices](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-pointing-devices/SKILL.md) for precision input.

name: apple-hig-multitasking
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting task continuity, background work, window focus, media interruptions, and simultaneous app use.

# Treat focus changes as continuity decisions

Read [the multitasking guide](../../references/multitasking.md). This workflow is application advice; do not collapse its visionOS media exception into a universal pause rule.

Inspect attention-dependent work, input-free background tasks, audio/video, saved state, target platform, and create/review/adapt request. Distinguish losing app activity, window focus, closing a window, and receiving an audio interruption. Record actual lifecycle handlers and completion sources.

Preserve context and finish eligible user-initiated input-free tasks before suspension. Notify only for important completion requiring another timely step; routine results can appear on return. Pause attention-dependent gameplay/media when appropriate, distinguishing sustained competing audio from brief directions and restoring only as justified. On iPad adapt to size without assuming access to the user's multitasking configuration. On Mac retain system key/main/layering cues. In visionOS looking at another window should not stop video merely because attention shifts; closing a Now Playing window pauses it, while closing a window backgrounds rather than quits the app. Shared Space and Full Space differ. The source does not define this mode on watchOS.

Implement lifecycle/resumption behavior or provide event-to-preservation/media/background-task contracts; reviews identify the exact event that loses work or wrongly stops/continues activity.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a spatial lecture pauses whenever someone looks at notes, while an unsent annotation disappears after closing its window. Decision: attention shift is not departure from video, and window closure is not app termination. After: let video continue on the documented focus change, preserve annotation state, and treat explicit Now Playing closure separately.

Deliver the artifact and lifecycle/event matrix with retained state and completion routes. Verify app switch, resize, competing audio, window close/reopen, and return. Fail for lost work, indiscriminate media pause/resume, or routine background completion spam. Native PiP/audio/lifecycle behavior and real background execution need runtime evidence.

Load [windows](../../../apple-hig-presentation/.topics/apple-hig-windows/SKILL.md), [playing-audio](../apple-hig-playing-audio/SKILL.md), or [playing-video](../apple-hig-playing-video/SKILL.md) for detailed handling.

name: apple-hig-layout
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting layout hierarchy, safe areas, size classes, resizable windows, enlarged text, or platform-specific spacing.
---

# Preserve relationships while available space changes

Read [Layout](../../references/layout.md). Inspect content priority, navigation, controls, supported environments, constraints, and current implementation. Identify design/review/adaptation mode and keep the existing layout system. Record actual available space and text/localization conditions; device names alone are insufficient evidence for a breakpoint.

Start with relationships: align peers, group related items, indent subordinates, and reveal secondary choices progressively. Place important content toward the leading/top region in the locale's reading order. Separate backgrounds that can extend beneath bars from important content/actions that must respect safe regions.

Choose adaptations from available width/height and environmental values, not a phone/tablet or portrait/landscape guess. Preserve selection, content, functionality, and idiom when columns collapse, actions overflow, or horizontal rows stack for larger text. Test the smallest and largest useful layouts first, then intermediate resizing, longer localization, direction changes, and display accommodations. Crop decorative backgrounds without distorting aspect ratio or hiding essential imagery.

Apply platform conditions deliberately: Mac essential controls cannot depend on a bottom edge that may be offscreen; TV content needs the guide's overscan insets and focus-expansion room; Watch normally needs very few side-by-side actions. visionOS windows/volumes should resize, use meaningful bounds, and avoid inline 3D crowding controls; use separate volumes for model-centric work. Read numeric platform specifications from the guide rather than generalizing one platform's spacing.

**Before → decision → after:** A reading list positions Delete at a fixed bottom coordinate and fixes each row to one line. Decision: resized windows and enlarged titles need flow-based layout. After, row height/wrapping adapt, secondary actions remain reachable through contextual overflow, and the selected article persists when the sidebar collapses.

Deliver corrected layouts/constraints or implementation plus an environment matrix. Fail if a required action disappears, related items detach, content overlaps hardware/bars, or resizing changes the task's meaning. Report tested dimensions/settings; static or Linux checks cannot establish native safe-area/focus behavior absent supported execution.

This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Use predictable relationships among content and controls while adapting to the actual available space. ## Visual hierarchy Prioritize important content toward the top and leading edge in reading order. Use system components for RTL adaptation. Align related items, indent subordinate items, and group relationships with space, containers, or separators. Reveal secondary choices progressively through disclosure, menus, nested views, or scrollable media sections. Distinguish navigation/controls with Liquid Glass and scroll-edge treatments; extend full-window backgrounds under bars and sidebars. A background extension effect can mirror and blur imagery under adjacent components instead of hiding essential original art. ## Adaptability Handle size classes, display sizes, orientation/aspect ratio, Dynamic Island, external displays, Display Zoom, resizable windows, text changes, localized length/direction/fonts, and date/number formats. Use SwiftUI or Auto Layout, safe areas, margins, and layout modifiers. Orientation-locked games must still resize. With large text, stack horizontal content, increase row height, and allow wrapping. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can supply Dynamic Type in games. Preview smallest/largest layouts first, then multiple devices, localizations, sizes, iPad resizing, and iPhone Mirroring. Scale backgrounds to fill without distorting aspect ratio; extreme wide/short or narrow/tall windows may crop much more than standard displays. ### Size classes Each axis is compact or regular, describing available width or height rather than device type or orientation. All four combinations can occur as apps resize, multitask, or mirror. Base layout on these environmental values, not idiom/orientation guesses. Preserve functionality across classes while changing how much is exposed, such as sidebar versus tabs or visible actions versus overflow. The platform idiom remains the same during resizing, so preserve its familiar character. ## Guides and safe areas Layout guides supply rectangular regions for alignment, spacing, margins, and readable text widths; custom guides can add app-specific structure. Safe areas exclude edge obstructions such as camera hardware, status bars, tab bars, and toolbars. Keep important content and controls within the appropriate safe regions. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS rules are listed. ### macOS Do not rely on the bottom of a window for essential controls because it may sit below the physical display. Avoid placing content behind the top camera housing. ### tvOS Inset primary content 60 pt vertically and 80 pt horizontally to withstand TV overscan/settings. Leave enough focus padding for system enlargement so focused items do not obscure important information. #### Grids Use consistent row/column spacing, sufficient room for enlargement, and symmetrical partial items at both horizontal edges. Add extra separation above and below row titles. UIKit collection flow layout derives the column count from item width and spacing. Source grid measurements follow; all use 40 pt horizontal gaps and a minimum 100 pt vertical gap between unfocused rows. #### Two-column grid Unfocused item width: 860 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Three-column grid Unfocused item width: 560 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Four-column grid Unfocused item width: 410 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Five-column grid Unfocused item width: 320 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Six-column grid Unfocused item width: 260 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Seven-column grid Unfocused item width: 217 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Eight-column grid Unfocused item width: 184 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Nine-column grid Unfocused item width: 160 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. ### visionOS Support resizing in windows and volumes; center content horizontally at very large sizes. Set minimum/maximum bounds only to avoid overlaps or unwieldy layouts, not to disable resizing. Use inline 3D content sparingly for meaningful additions; inset it so it avoids controls and window edges. Prefer volumes or immersive spaces for large/model-centric content. Open supplemental content in an adjacent window, reserving ornaments for interactive app controls. Space controls so hover feedback remains distinct; regular buttons should have centers at least 60 pt apart. ### watchOS Normally use no more than three glyph buttons or two text buttons side by side. Full-width text controls usually work best; two short labels can fit on a non-scrolling screen. Support autorotation when people may show content, such as a photo or QR code, to another person or reader instead of always sleeping on wrist-away movement. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 9, 2026, September 9, 2025, June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, September 9, 2024, June 10, 2024, February 2, 2024, December 5, 2023, September 15, 2023, June 21, 2023, September 14, 2022.

# Windows Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/windows) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Primary windows host app navigation, content, and actions. Auxiliary windows focus on one task or area and typically close after that task. iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS windows establish content boundaries and enable multitasking with system movement, sizing, and closing controls. ## Best practices Adapt smoothly to size changes. Open new windows when preserving context or working in parallel helps, without generating clutter by default. Offer Open in New Window in a context or File menu when useful. Retain system frames and controls instead of imitating them. Call the experience a window in user-facing copy; scene is an implementation term. ## Platform considerations This multiwindow component guidance marks iOS, tvOS, and watchOS unsupported. ### iPadOS People choose fullscreen or windowed behavior in Multitasking & Gestures settings. Fullscreen fills the display and uses app switching; windowed mode supports multiple resizable, movable windows with remembered placement. Move leading toolbar items inward when window controls appear so they do not overlap. Consider gestures to open content in a new window, such as expanding a collection item with a pinch. Quick Look can present a single file without a custom window if the app supports multiple windows. ### macOS Support normal movement, resize, minimization, and frequent switching among multiple apps' windows. Games also need the appropriate system game-window configuration. #### macOS window anatomy A frame above the body supplies movement, window controls, and optionally a toolbar. Edges normally resize. A rare bottom bar is also part of the frame. #### macOS window states An app has one main window; the system has one key/input window at a time. A floating panel can be key while its document stays main. Dock activation brings app windows forward but makes only the recently used one key. Other windows are inactive. Colored close/minimize/zoom controls identify key state; inactive and non-key main windows use gray, and inactive windows lose vibrancy. Some panels take key status only through the title bar or keyboard-input controls. Custom rendering must preserve these automatic state cues. Avoid critical controls at the bottom, which may be offscreen; reserve bottom bars for small contextual summaries, using an inspector for more detail. ### visionOS Windows and volumetric windows can each contain 2D/3D content and coexist in Shared or Full Space. Plain style omits the glass plane. The system positions the first opened surface, then people can move it. #### visionOS windows Default windows use an upright glass plane with close, move, and resize controls, and can add Share, tabs, toolbars, and ornaments. Dynamic scale preserves apparent size across distance. Prefer familiar windows for familiar tasks, reserving immersion for meaningful content. Retain the glass background: it adapts to surroundings and communicates scale and position; removing it weakens legibility and grouping, while an opaque replacement conceals surroundings. Default initial size is 1280×720 pt, placed about 2 meters ahead with an apparent width of about 3 meters. Avoid excess empty space and choose a shape suited to content. Set minimum/maximum sizes and adapt layout throughout. Keep 3D depth shallow in a window because content too far from its surface is clipped; use a volume for deeper objects. #### visionOS volumes Volumes show bounded content from multiple angles; close and move controls turn to face the viewer. Prefer them for rich 3D scenes over UI-centric interfaces. Pin 2D overlays to 3D content with attachments and test multiple viewpoints. Dynamic scaling usually improves distant legibility and interaction, but fixed scaling (the default) suits true-to-life products. From visionOS 2, a baseplate border glow on look reveals bounds and resize controls when content does not fill them. Full-bleed content or a custom baseplate may not need it. Volumes can have an ornament alongside toolbar/tabs: use attachment anchors to keep its position viewer-relative, place it on another edge, and usually add only one. Choose a floor-parallel alignment for largely viewed objects, or a viewer-tilting alignment when interactive content should remain usable while reclining. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) [Split views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/split-views) [Multitasking](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/multitasking) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 9, 2025, June 10, 2024, June 21, 2023.

# Playing audio Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-audio) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Respect the person's selected output, volume, and silence state. Silent mode suppresses incidental feedback/game soundtracks but permits deliberately initiated media, alarms, and messages. System volume governs output, with separate iPhone ringer settings. Connecting headphones should reroute smoothly; disconnecting them should pause playback for privacy. ## Best practices Adjust relative mix levels without changing global volume. Permit output rerouting and use the system volume view with its output chooser. Select an audio-session category that fits the importance of sound and coexistence with other audio: | Category | Silent switch | Mixing | Background | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Solo ambient | Respected | No | No | | Ambient | Respected | Yes | No | | Playback | Ignored for essential audio | Configurable | Playback supported | | Record | Ignored | No | Recording supported | | Play and record | Ignored | Configurable | Both supported | Solo ambient suits nonessential exclusive sound; ambient lets external music coexist; playback suits media/learning; recording apps may switch to playback to review; play-and-record suits calls or messaging. Respond to external playback controls only while playing or in an appropriate audio/output context, without stealing another app's audio. Never repurpose unsupported controls. Custom players should solve needs beyond standard commands, such as unusual skip intervals or related content. When a temporary interruption ends, deactivate with notification so other apps can resume. ## Handling interruptions Choose interruption policy deliberately for recording/calls. For recording or other audio work that should continue, the app can ask the system to leave current audio uninterrupted by an incoming call unless the person accepts that call. For example, a closed iPad Smart Folio mutes the microphone and interrupts a VoIP session; end the call rather than automatically unmuting on reopen. Distinguish resumable interruptions such as calls from nonresumable choices such as a newly started playlist. A media player should resume automatically only when appropriate and signaled; a game's incidental sound can follow its gameplay resumption without the same explicit-playback check. ## Platform considerations ### iOS, iPadOS Use system sound services for short sounds and vibrations. ### macOS Notification audio mixes with other sound by default. ### tvOS Audio is initiated by interaction or device calibration, rather than automatic sounds for alerts or notifications. ### visionOS Use meaningful sound to help navigation and spatial understanding, while always providing an alternative for essential information. Native controls already provide sounds; custom objects need appropriate feedback too. Spatial Audio can combine environmental ambience and localized moving or stationary sources, following a moved window. Avoid repetitive fatigue with subtle pitch/level variation, which can be randomized from one asset. Tracked sound normally reinforces an object's changing position/distance; wearer-fixed sound can suit an enveloping experience. Now Playing audio pauses when its window closes; other audio may duck when attention moves to another app. ### watchOS System-managed short clips can play in the foreground; longer audio can continue after wrist lowering or app switching. Encode audio as 64 kbps HE-AAC for quality at low data size. A system Now Playing view controls current/recent audio, including another watch/iPhone source, and automatically selects the relevant source. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Playing video](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-video) [Feedback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback) #### Developer documentation — AVFoundation — AVFAudio — MusicKit #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 21, 2023.

# iPad document comparator: continuity specification

Platform: iPadOS. Compare and edit two documents without losing work when the available window size, active window, or foreground app changes. This revises the supplied behavior: narrowing must not close the app, backgrounding must not clear edits, and returning must not start audio.

## State ownership and persistence

- Document state is keyed by stable document ID: content, revision, unsaved edits, and undo/redo history. A comparison workspace holds the two document IDs, comparison options, selected difference, and pending comparison revision pair.
- Each window has its own stable restoration ID, workspace/document route, active document, selection/caret, scroll anchor for each document, zoom, and editing focus target. Switching windows must never send edits or Undo to the previously active document.
- Persist edits incrementally through a durable local journal; checkpoint window/workspace state after meaningful changes and on deactivation/backgrounding. Do not rely on a final lifecycle callback to save work. Treat accepted edits as recoverable only once journaled; surface a persistence failure and retain the in-memory draft with retry instead of claiming it is saved.
- Persist restoration records atomically with a schema version and document revision references. Restore drafts before starting a new comparison. Recover the latest valid checkpoint plus journal after process termination; do not restore a stale comparison as current.
- Preserve selection, anchors and undo history during live resize, window switching and background/foreground transitions. On relaunch, restore persisted history and anchors where their revisions remain valid; clamp an invalid anchor to the nearest surviving location. If a file is missing or permission is unavailable, retain its draft and workspace identity, explain the issue, and offer retry/relink without silently substituting another document.

## Adaptive comparison flow

Use available content bounds after safe areas, system window controls and keyboard avoidance, rather than orientation, device name, or an assumed multitasking setting. Retain system resize/move/close controls and keep leading app actions clear of them.

Product layout rule (not an Apple numerical requirement): show two editors side by side when each can receive at least 320 pt of usable width after the divider and surrounding controls. Below that, show one editor with always reachable “Document A” and “Document B” switches, filenames, active-document indication, and previous/next difference actions. Keep both document models alive; switching restores each editor's caret, draft and scroll anchor. Each difference retains its paired location so the other document can be reached in one switch. If vertical space is short, allow the editor to scroll and move secondary actions to reachable overflow. Never exit or discard a workspace to enforce the two-column layout.

On widening, restore both editors and their independent positions. Layout changes alone must not move the selected difference, change active document, commit/cancel editing, reset undo, dismiss the workspace, or start playback. Editing, switching documents and navigating differences must work with touch alone; attached keyboard commands must target the active editor and survive accessory changes. No essential action depends on hover.

## Event and recovery contract

| Event | Retained state and behavior | Completion/return behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resize or rotate, including while typing | Reflow existing workspace; preserve both drafts, selection, scroll anchors and undo | Continue editing the same document; no restart or audio event |
| Another app/window gains activity | Checkpoint current context; preserve document models and pending input | Return to the same route and editor; restore editing target when available without forcing the keyboard open |
| App backgrounds / system may suspend | Journal edits; checkpoint; finish eligible user-initiated input-free save/comparison work only within system-granted execution | If interrupted, resume/recompute from saved revisions on return; no promise of unlimited background work |
| Comparison completes while inactive | Store result with its input revision pair | Show result/status on return; discard/recompute stale results; no routine completion sound or notification |
| User closes one window | Save its restoration record and drafts; stop its playback | Other windows continue independently; reopening restores that window's context |
| Process terminates and app relaunches | Recover durable documents, drafts and workspace records | Restore context, show pending/retry state for unfinished work, and remain silent |
| Save or comparison fails | Keep drafts and last valid result, clearly distinguish pending/error from saved/current | Offer retry; never clear edits to recover |

## Independent document windows

On supported iPadOS configurations, offer “Open in New Window” for either document. A primary document window is independently editable and has its own document identity and window context. Opening B must not replace A, redirect A's undo history, or close the comparison workspace. Normal Open reuses an existing window for that document when present; repeated Open in New Window requests for that document activate its existing dedicated editor rather than accumulating duplicates. The comparison workspace can still show the same document through a shared, revisioned document model, so committed edits propagate to comparison results without creating divergent unsaved copies. Serialize edits per document; focus-local Undo operates on the active document's history.

Closing A's window does not close B's window or delete A. Reopen restores A's saved context. Let the system manage window placement and activation; never infer the user's multitasking configuration. Where separate windows are unavailable, keep both documents independently editable through the comparison window's document switcher and preserve their state. Supported OS versions and multiwindow configuration require implementation verification.

## Audio contract

The supplied brief does not identify a useful audio feature. The comparator is silent by default: no startup, restoration, comparison-completion or focus-change sound. Neither activation nor restored playback state is a Play command.

If an existing explicit read-aloud/preview feature is retained, require a visible Play/Pause control. Track playback position separately from document state. For this reading/editing task, pause on leaving the app, closing the owning window, headphone disconnection, or a sustained competing audio interruption; keep position and require explicit Play to resume. A brief interruption may duck ongoing user-started audio only while the app remains active and the system permits it; if paused, return paused. This conservative resume policy is a product choice, not a universal HIG requirement. Respect selected output, system volume and silence behavior; never change global volume or take another app's external playback controls. Use a category appropriate to deliberate spoken playback only if that feature exists; do not configure a playback session merely to restore a document. No recording is specified.

## Guidance basis

The retention and background-work contract follows [Multitasking — Best practices and iPadOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/multitasking). Adaptive layouts follow [Designing for iPadOS — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ipados) and [Layout — Adaptability and Size classes](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout). Explicit parallel windows and preserved system controls follow [Windows — Best practices and iPadOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/windows). Audio intent, routing and interruption distinctions follow [Playing audio — Best practices and Handling interruptions](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-audio). Links identify official sources; this specification uses only installed local guidance, with no web verification.
EOF"
